requirement:
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate. They exercise each obligation of `requirements.references.outlines` with concrete assertions. I read only the test code and some implementation snippets. I did not read the implementation to decide correctness.

- **Seven languages and extension selection (case-insensitive):**
  - `src/outline/tests.rs#fn[profiles_are_selected_by_extension_case_insensitively]` asserts the profile chosen for upper- and mixed-case extensions of Rust, Python, TSX, Markdown and TOML.
  - The same test asserts that `notes` and `notes.rs.txt` fall back to plain text.
  - Per-language tests parse real sources for Rust, Python, TypeScript and TSX, CSS, Markdown, TOML and YAML (`.yml`).
- **Pinned grammars and deliberate upgrades:** `fn[grammar_dependencies_are_pinned_to_exact_versions]` requires every `tree-sitter-*` dependency in `Cargo.toml` to be an exact `=x.y.z` pin.
- **Syntax errors fail and report the first error's line:** `fn[reports_parse_failures_with_lines]` covers these cases.
  - A Rust error reports the line of the broken declaration, not an earlier one.
  - A Python error fails to parse.
  - A TOML source with an early error and a later error reports the earlier line, with the `line N: ` prefix, so the *first* error wins.
  - Only Rust, Python and TOML are tested. I saw no per-language conditional in `check_errors`, so the other grammars share the same code path.
- **Plain-text profile:** `fn[plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes]` and the `src/authoring/tools.rs` outline test check these points.
  - Blank lines are skipped.
  - Every node has kind `line`, no name and a `line@…` selector.
  - Identical lines share a selector.
  - Whitespace inside a line is normalised.
- **Per-language mapping with named or anonymous nodes:**
  - **Rust:** `fn[rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry]`, `fn[selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates]` and `fn[item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not]` cover Rust. They check named and anonymous items such as `use@` and `macro@`. Expression macros inside function bodies are not nodes.
  - **Python:** `fn[python_profile_outlines_defs_classes_and_statements]` covers Python, including the decorator and leading-comment line range.
  - **TypeScript and TSX:** `fn[typescript_profile_outlines_declarations]`.
  - **CSS:** `fn[css_profile_names_rules_by_normalized_selectors]`.
  - **Markdown:** `fn[markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading]` covers an anonymous pre-heading section and nested sections.
  - **TOML and YAML:** `fn[toml_and_yaml_profiles_name_keys]` covers both, including anonymous `item@` nodes.
- **Only mapped kinds appear, and unmapped nodes are transparent:** these tests show unmapped kinds leave the outline, with their mapped descendants nested under the nearest mapped ancestor.
  - The Rust test shows `fn[inner]` under `fn[outer]`.
  - The CSS test shows `rule` under `media`.
  - The TypeScript test shows `class[C]/method[m]`.
  - The YAML test shows `pair/item@/pair`.
  - `@import` is not an outline node in CSS.
- **Root node, and unmapped source belongs to the root with no fallback kinds:**
  - Resolving the empty selector to the root is asserted for Rust.
  - `fn[file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root]` covers Rust inner docs and Markdown front matter.
  - The Python test checks that top-level `import` and `if` map to the root.
  - `fn[no_profile_invents_fallback_kinds]` checks all seven profiles. It asserts no `stmt`, `block`, `node` or `item` kinds and no extra nodes for unmapped code.
- **Comments are not outline nodes:** the CSS, Markdown, TOML, YAML, Python and Rust summaries and selector lists contain no comment nodes.
- **Attached siblings count toward line range and hash:** the Python decorator is included in the `def[f]` range. Other tests in the same file check attached Rust attributes and doc comments. Those tests belong to other requirements (`selector_duplicate_names`, the hash tests). Attachment is a `MAY`, so I treat this as adequately covered.
- **Profiles documented:** `fn[every_profile_mapping_is_documented]` checks every profile's extensions and every kind→grammar row against the table in `md/reference.md`. It also checks the plain-text row.
- **Outline tool and redaction:** `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[outline_lists_nested_nodes_without_text_or_inputs]` and `src/redaction/tests.rs#fn[redaction_never_changes_an_outline]` show that the outline output has the required shape and is unaffected by redaction.

I found no unrequired-behavior gap. The untested corners are error cases in grammars other than Rust, Python and TOML, and whitespace-only lines in plain text. They are not distinct obligations beyond what the tests already show.
